source_text: Rideo autem, cum infirmitas carnis opponitur, quae summa fortitudo dicenda est. Iterum nubere, est res virium; resurgere in opera carnis de continentiae otio, substantia est laterum. Talis infirmitas, et tertio, et quarto, et usque septimo forsitan matrimonio sufficit; ut quae totiens fortior, quotiens fuerit infirmior, habitura jam non Apostolum auctorem, sed Hermogenem aliquem, plures solitum mulieres ducere quam pingere, materia enim in illo abundat, unde et animam esse praesumens, multo magis spiritum a Deo non habet, jam nec psychicus, quia non de afflatu Dei psychicus. Quid, si inopiam quis causetur, ut carnem suam aperte prostitutam profiteatur, exhibitionis causa nubentem, oblitus de victu et vestitu non esse cogitandum? Habet Deum etiam corvorum educatorem, etiam florum excultorem. Quid si solitudinem domus obtendat? Quasi una mulier frequentiam praestet homini ad fugam proximo: habet viduam utique, quam adsumat licebit. Non unam generis hujus uxorem, sed etiam plures habere concessum est. Quid, si de posteritate quis cogitet iisdem animis, quibus oculis uxor Loth, ut ideo quis repetat matrimonium, quia de priore liberos non habuit; haeredes scilicet christianus quaeret, saeculi totius exhaeres? Habet fratres, habet Ecclesiam matrem. Aliud est, si et apud Christum legibus Juliis agi credunt, et existimant caelibes et orbos ex testamento Dei solidum non posse capere. Nubant igitur hujusmodi in finem usque, ut in ista confusione carnis; sicut Sodoma et Gomorrha, et diluvii dies, ab illo ultimo exitu saeculi deprehendantur. Adjiciant tertium dictum: Manducemus, et bibamus, et nubamus: cras enim moriemur; non recogitantes Vae illud praegnantibus et lactantibus, multo gravius et amarius eventurum in concussione totius mundi, quam evenit in vastatione unius particulae Judaeae. Satis opportunos novissimis temporibus fructus iteratis matrimoniis colligant, ubera fluitantia, et uteros nauseantes, et infantes pipiantes. Parent Antichristo in quae libidinosius saeviat. Adducet illis carnifices obstetrices.
pass_a_gloss: I laugh, however, when the weakness of the flesh is opposed, which is to be said the greatest strength. To marry again is a matter of strength; to rise again in the works of the flesh from the leisure of continence is a substance of loins. Such weakness is sufficient, and for a third, and fourth, and perhaps up to a seventh marriage; so that which is stronger as many times as it is weaker, will already have not the Apostle as author, but some Hermogenes, accustomed to lead more women than to paint, for in him the material abounds, from which he also presumes to have a soul, much more does he not have the Spirit from God, already not psychic, because not from the breath of God is he psychic. What if someone should cause poverty, so that he openly professes his flesh to be prostituted, marrying for the sake of exhibition, forgetful that it is not to be thought about for food and clothing? He has God as the educator of ravens, also the cultivator of flowers. What if he should offer the solitude of his house? As if one woman should provide a crowd for a man to flee to his neighbor: he has a widow, whom he will be allowed to take. Not one wife of this kind is permitted, but also several. What if someone should think about posterity with the same minds as Lot's wife, so that someone repeats marriage because he did not have children from the previous one; surely a Christian seeks heirs, disinherited from the whole world? He has brothers, he has the Church as mother. It is different if they also believe that among Christ's laws the laws of Julius are in effect, and they think that the celibate and the orphan cannot receive a solid thing from God's testament. Therefore, they marry to this end, until in this confusion of the flesh; just as Sodom and Gomorrah, and the days of the flood, are caught from that last exit of the world. Let them add the third statement: Let us eat, and drink, and marry; for tomorrow we will die; not considering that woe to those who are pregnant and nursing, will be much more serious and bitter in the shaking of the whole world, than it happened in the devastation of one part of Judea. They gather the fruits of repeated marriages at the most opportune times for the last times, overflowing breasts, and nauseating wombs, and crying infants. They prepare for the Antichrist in which he rages more licentiously. He will bring to them executioners and midwives.

pass_b_english: I laugh when the weakness of the flesh is set up as an objection, weakness that ought to be called the greatest strength (1 Cor 7). To marry again is a show of strength; to resume the works of the flesh after the rest of continence is a matter of loin-power. Such weakness suffices for a third, a fourth, and perhaps up to a seventh marriage; so that the more often it is weaker, the stronger it becomes — and will end up claiming not the Apostle as its author, but some Hermogenes, a man used to leading more women than painting them; for in him the raw material abounds, from which he even presumes to have a soul, and therefore all the more he does not have the Spirit from God; he is not even psychical, because he is not psychical from the breath of God (1 Cor 2:14-15). What if someone pleads poverty, so that he openly admits he is prostituting his flesh, marrying for display, forgetting that food and clothing are not to be anxious concerns? He has God as the feeder of ravens and the dresser of flowers (Matt 6:26-30). What if he puts forward the loneliness of his house? As if one woman could supply a crowd for a man to flee to his neighbor; he has a widow, after all, whom he is permitted to take. Not just one wife of this sort is allowed, but several. What if someone thinks about posterity with the same mindset as Lot’s wife, so that he repeats marriage because he had no children from the first; surely a Christian seeks heirs, though disinherited from the whole world? He has brothers; he has the Church as mother. It is another matter if they also believe that the Julian laws operate under Christ, and think that the celibate and the childless cannot receive a solid inheritance from God’s testament. So they marry to that very end, until in this confusion of flesh they are caught at the world’s final exit, just as Sodom and Gomorrah and the days of the flood were (Luke 17:26-30). Let them add the third saying: ‘Let us eat and drink and marry, for tomorrow we die’ (1 Cor 15:32; Isa 22:13) — not recalling that woe to the pregnant and the nursing will be far more severe and bitter in the shaking of the whole world than it was in the devastation of one part of Judea (Matt 24:19; Isa 13:6, 8). They gather the ripe fruits of repeated marriages for the last times: breasts overflowing, wombs heaving, infants wailing. They prepare recruits for the Antichrist, that he may rage more wantonly. He will bring them executioners and midwives.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A provides a literal gloss, while Pass B provides a more fluent rendering with appropriate scriptural identifications for the allusions (e.g., 1 Cor 7, 1 Cor 2:14-15, Matt 6:26-30, Luke 17:26-30, 1 Cor 15:32, Isa 22:13, Matt 24:19, Isa 13:6, 8). All clauses, including the complex description of Hermogenes and the apocalyptic imagery, are preserved.
